title: TaskScope context propagation: structured tracing, MDC and ScopedValue
requirement: ADR-0012 (ScopedValue request context, structured concurrency); decision recorded 2026-09-26: always propagate OpenTelemetry context and MDC, a span per scope and per subtask always on, ScopedValue by declared keys; plan §20 item RT-02; register Section J
acceptance: The scope span is a child of the owner's current span; subtask spans are children of the scope span; spans started inside a subtask are children of the subtask span
Spans record quorus.taskscope.outcome: success; failed with the exception and ERROR status; cancelled for siblings; timeout with ERROR status on the scope span
Subtask log events carry the owner's MDC; the subtask MDC traceId and spanId equal the subtask span; subtask MDC changes do not leak into the owner or later subtasks
Declared ScopedValue keys bound in the owner are re-bound in subtasks; undeclared keys are not; a declared key the owner has not bound stays unbound
classification: unit and component (real OpenTelemetry SDK with in-memory exporter; real logback appender)

test.synchronisation: CompletableFuture handshakes and interruption only; no sleeps, no polling; preemptive 10-second timeout per test

discardedAttempts.reason: Test defect: logback evaluates an event's MDC lazily and ListAppender does not freeze it, so the MDC assertions read the owner thread's MDC. Two MDC tests passed falsely. A probe confirmed that LogbackMDCAdapter uses a plain ThreadLocal and a new virtual thread sees no MDC. Fixed with a real logback appender that calls prepareForDeferredProcessing().

red.revision: 341a509 plus a compiling Builder skeleton (tracer and inherit accepted but ignored) and the 11 new tests
red.result: 8 of 11 new tests failed for missing behaviour: no scope or subtask spans; the owner MDC and trace IDs absent in subtask log events; the declared tenant unbound. 3 new tests passed as intended guards that must hold before and after the change: undeclared keys not inherited, an unbound key stays unbound, no MDC leakage. The 10 existing TaskScopeTest tests passed.

green.change: TaskScope starts a scope span at open under Context.current(); each subtask runs in a child span made current, records outcome, exception and status, installs a copy of the owner's MDC plus its own traceId and spanId, clears the MDC on exit, and re-binds the ScopedValue bindings captured at open; close() ends the scope span with success, failed, timeout or cancelled

refactor: open(name, timeout) delegates to the builder, removing duplicated validation

processDeviation.description: Behaviour implemented during green without a preceding failing test is covered by tests classified as retrospective characterization under plan §6.1.
processDeviation.testDefectFound: The first version of ownerInterruptedWhileCloseWaitsKeepsWaitingAndRestoresTheInterrupt hung. The owner could call close() before the subtask thread ran, so TaskScope correctly skipped the task and the test's handshake never completed. Fixed with a start handshake. This shows the start-of-run cancellation guard does fire in real races.

regression.result: 1,548 tests, 0 failures; JaCoCo gate met. TaskScope 126/126 lines and 52/52 branches; SubtaskImpl 63/64 lines and 17/18 branches; Builder and Binding 100%

limitations: The one uncovered line is the start-of-run cancellation guard, which is hit only when cancellation races thread start. It cannot be triggered deterministically without a test hook in production code.
The log of the first successful core verify after green was overwritten by the next run before it was renamed; the retained logs are the failed race run and the final successful run.
No production code uses TaskScope yet; the first consumer arrives with RT-03. Consumers must declare their request-context ScopedValue keys.
sensitiveDataCheck: Logs contain Maven and test output only; no request bodies, credentials, keys or sensitive payloads.
